text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.title: Disc Jockey
text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.disab: Will force notes to play synchronously with client ticks instead of in a separate thread.
This can lead to performance loss, especially when you client has low or inconsistent fps but can fix issues when playback does not happen at all.
text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.omnid: Makes all note block sounds when playing a song omnidirectional, creating a more pleasing listening experience
If you don't know what that means, I recommend you just try it and hear the difference
text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.expec: Select the server version, you expect this mod to be used on.
This affects how reachable NoteBlocks are determined.
Selecting the wrong version could cause you not to be able to play some distant note blocks which could break/worsen playback
If you're unsure, or play on many different server versions and don't mind not reaching every possible note block, select "All"
text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.delay: Delays playback for specified seconds, after tuning finished, if any (e.g. 0.5 for half a second delay).

text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.packe: While a song plays the mod sends note block interaction packets. As long as the rate shown in the song selection screen stays at or below this many packets per second it is drawn green.
Up to this many packets per second the rate is drawn yellow, above it red. Should not be lower than the green threshold.
disc_jockey.lyrics.selector_not_allowed: Disc Jockey: this server does not allow target selectors, so each private lyric line is now sent with one command per player.
disc_jockey.lyrics.dm_warning:
Disc Jockey: %s players are inside the private message radius.

Without operator permissions Minecraft only lets /msg address one player at a time, so every lyric line costs one command per player, and it disconnects players who send much more than about one command per second.

Only the closest players up to the configured private message burst receive a line - at most nine - and lines that do not fit that budget are skipped completely instead of reaching only some players. Lines are also spaced at least %s seconds apart. Raise the burst in the settings to reach more players, or use public chat output instead?
text.autoconfig.disc_jockey.option.lyric: Minecraft disconnects players who send chat messages or commands faster than roughly once per second, so lyrics are throttled to at least this delay.
Players within this many blocks receive the lyrics when public chat output is off. Maximum 40.

At most this many players are served in private mode, nearest first, and never more than the configured private message burst. Every recipient costs one command, and without operator permissions Minecraft allows only about one command per second with a short burst, so a line is skipped when the budget is used up.

How many private message commands may be sent back to back for one lyric line. Minecraft kicks a player without operator permissions who sends ten commands inside its spam window, so nine is the absolute maximum. The default of eight assumes the stock server setting of ten seconds (command-spam-threshold-seconds); on a stricter server, lower it.
Command used for private lyrics. Some servers disable or rename /msg.
Sends a single command that addresses everyone in range, but most servers only allow target selectors for operators.
When the server refuses it, private lyrics automatically fall back to one command per player.
disc_jockey.screen.lyrics.tooltip: Send the lyrics of the playing song into chat. The preview at the bottom always shows them, whether this is on or not.
disc_jockey.screen.lyrics.public.tooltip: Checked: lyrics go to public chat. Unchecked: they are only sent to the players near you.
disc_jockey.screen.lyrics.offset.earlier: Show the lyrics half a second earlier and shift every timestamp in the .lrc file by the same amount, so the change is kept.
disc_jockey.screen.lyrics.offset.later.t: Show the lyrics half a second later and shift every timestamp in the .lrc file by the same amount, so the change is kept.
